headToHead.voiceNote: Cover the names and Liam is Liam in every line by syntax alone: formal clauses on trivial things ('encountered a culinary block', 'supposing I were to actually acquire'), 'friend', a self-aware plea at the end. Cover Dash's names and his best lines are identifiable mostly by topic (platforms, conversions, the jacket). The sentence shape (four to six full-stop fragments, punch, optional tag) is the house staccato; Crumb's notifications and Nav's clipped imperatives are built of the same bricks. With startup words cut to seasoning, nothing in the grammar says Dash. Bar.
headToHead.constructionNote: Dash's best twelve are tighter than Liam's (Liam runs to 25 to 27 words) and the turns are real: 'together on the fifth', 'The good sleeve', 'Date it whenever' land on the last words. But too many lines add a sentence after the punch that explains or cheers it ('Nobody does that deliberately.', 'Still stunning.', 'Exhausting.'), and the downward-pivot ladder and the counting tag repeat until the turn is predictable. Liam's lines each do one move once. Tie, leaning bar.
headToHead.quotableNote: 'Together on the fifth', 'the good sleeve', 'click rate is lawsuits' and 'back for an umbrella' would clip. Liam's 180/360 line and 'into existing before it was cool' are the famous ones, and the narrator lines on him ('a cloud of mist and angst') are better than any Dash rival line. Tie.
headToHead.verdict: The bar is the better written character: Liam wins voice outright, and Dash only draws construction and quotability.

biggestGap: Dash has no sentence shape of his own: with the startup words cut to seasoning, almost every line is four to six full-stop fragments plus a trailing tag, the same staccato Crumb and Nav speak in, so covered lines read as 'a sad suitor' rather than 'Dash'. Next pass, rewrite his stage lines as one fast run-on of salesman inference chained with commas and 'so' ('They blocked me on four platforms, so I'm still on the fifth, so we're basically together'), the conclusion on the last words and nothing after it, and keep the full-stop fragments only for the confessions, where the hype is meant to drop.
